data.gender_notes: Areesh is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'ra's' meaning 'night' or 'darkness'. In Islamic traditions, it symbolizes the eternal protection of Allah (swt) in the darkest hours of the night. The name Areesh carries the meaning “Night or Darkness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Areesh usually hope their child will grow to embody night or darkness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies Allah's (swt) protection and guidance in times of darkness.
data.etymology: Areesh belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night or Darkness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Areesh total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: عريش
in_arabic.long_meaning: العريش هو مصدر فعل عَرَشَ، ومعناهُ المكان الذي يُحصد من شَعره، وهو كذلك مصدر فعل عَرَشَةَ، ومعناهُ الحصاد من شَعره، والمصدر أيضًا يُشير إلى العُريش، وهو نوع من الحشائش، وفي القرآن الكريم، يُشير العريش إلى الحصاد من شَعرة، ويكون بمعنى عريش السحر، وهو نوع من الحشائش التي يُستخدم في الحصاد، وفي اللغة العربية، يُشير العريش إلى ما يَحصد من شَعرة، ومنه قول الله تعالى، "وَإِنَّا لَمُنشِئوُنَ الَّذِي يَشُقُّ الْأَرْضَ وَتَنشِقُ فَتُثَقِّفُ وَجُزٍ عَريشَ السَّحَرِ" (سورة الحاقة، الآية 5)

In Islamic tradition, the name Areesh is associated with the concept of spiritual purification and renewal. It is believed to represent a state of being free from worldly attachments and desires, and is often seen as a symbol of spiritual growth and maturity. In Arabic, the root of the name Areesh is 'r-sh', which means to cut or to harvest. The name Areesh is also mentioned in the Quran, where it refers to the act of cutting the hair of the prophets. In Islamic tradition, cutting the hair is seen as a way of symbolizing spiritual renewal and purification.
